key_insight: Composition anisotropy in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics enables an unusually large bulk photovoltaic field along the non-polar vertical direction, far exceeding the polar in-plane response.
engineering_relevance: This opens a path to high-performance voltage-readout photodetectors and other optoelectronic devices that exploit directional photovoltaic anisotropy rather than conventional polarization alignment.
method: Analyze bulk photovoltaic effect (BPE) in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics.
Link the strong vertical response to shift-current BPE plus coupling between inorganic photocarrier generation and insulating organic layers.
Develop formulas for laser-intensity- and dimension-dependent photovoltage scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the vertical EBPE is up to two orders of magnitude larger than the polar in-plane direction and up to orders of magnitude higher than benchmark photoferroelectrics, with the highest value reported for 2D HPFs so far.
watch_item: The unusually strong response depends on specific compositional anisotropy and layered structure, so device performance may be sensitive to material uniformity, thickness, and orientation control.
paper_title: Composition Anisotropy Drives Large Bulk Photovoltaic Fields Along the Non-polar Vertical Direction in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectrics
